title: The great difference between Christians and people of the world
english: There is a great change between Christians and the people of the world. Those who have the spirit of the world are bound in heart and in mind to earthly bonds. But Christians long for the love of the heavenly Father, and they keep Him alone before their eyes with much desire.

The world of Christians is another world, and their conduct is another, and their mind is another, and their word is another, and their action is another. The conduct, mind, word, and action of the people of the world is other, and the conduct, mind, word, and action of Christians is other. Those people are one thing, and these are another. The difference between them is great.

The people of the world are bound to earthly things, but Christians long for the love of the heavenly Father. They keep Him alone before their eyes with much desire. The world of Christians is another, and their conduct, mind, word, and action is other.

orientation: Macarius opens his homily by contrasting true Christians with people of this world, before urging believers to acquire the heavenly garment through faith and virtuous living.

title: The heavenly garment must be acquired now
english: Let us strive, then, through faith and virtuous conduct to acquire that garment from here, so that, having clothed the body, we may not be found naked, and there may be nothing to glorify our flesh on that day. For each person, to the degree that he was deemed worthy through faith and diligence to become a partaker of the Holy Spirit, to that same degree his body also will be glorified on that day. What the soul has stored up within now will then be uncovered and appear outside the body.

Just as the trees, when winter has passed and an invisible power from the sun and the winds warms them from within, put forth and send out leaves like garments, and flowers, and fruits—so too the flowers of the grass in that season come forth from within the earth, and the earth is covered and clothed, and the grass is like the lilies, about which the Lord said, “Not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these” (Matthew 6:29; Luke 12:27). For all these things are examples, and types, and images of the things to come.

So for all God-loving souls—that is, for true Christians—the first month is the month called April, which is the day of the resurrection. And through the power of the sun of righteousness, the glory of the Holy Spirit comes forth from within, covering and sheltering the bodies of the saints—that glory which they had hidden within their souls. For what a person has now, that same thing comes forth outside the body then.

This month, I say, is the first of the months of the year. This month brings joy to all creation. This month clothes the naked trees and opens the earth. This month brings joy to all living creatures. This month displays cheerfulness to all. This is the first month for Christians—the month called April, which is the season of the resurrection, in which their bodies will be glorified through the ineffable light that is in them even now, that is, through the power of the Holy Spirit. That Spirit will then be to them garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, and eternal life. For all the beauty of heavenly brightness and loveliness the Spirit of the Godhead will then become theirs.
Therefore each of us ought to believe and strive.
